item_description: An Australian government center that coordinates cyber threat information and provides security guidance to organizations and the public.
item_facts: The ACSC is part of the Australian Signals Directorate.
It publishes alerts and guidance on cyber threats.
Its organizational structure and services can change over time.
needs_review: Verify current remit and organizational placement on official Australian government sites.

item_description: Canada’s national technical authority for cyber security, operating within the Communications Security Establishment.
item_facts: The Centre provides cyber security advice and guidance.
It issues alerts and reports on cyber threats.
It supports government, critical infrastructure and other organizations.
needs_review: Verify current organizational remit and public services on official Canadian sources.

item_description: India’s national computer emergency response team, responsible for coordinating responses to cyber security incidents.
item_facts: CERT-In operates under India’s Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
It issues cyber security advisories and incident-related directions.
Its statutory role is defined under India’s Information Technology Act and rules.
needs_review: Verify current legal and operational remit using official CERT-In and MeitY materials.

item_description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, which leads national efforts to strengthen cyber and infrastructure security.
item_facts: CISA is an agency of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security.
Its work includes cyber defense and critical infrastructure resilience.
CISA operates the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
needs_review: Verify current remit, catalog operations and organizational status on CISA.gov.

item_description: The European Union Agency for Cybersecurity, supporting cooperation and cyber resilience across EU member states.
item_facts: ENISA is an agency of the European Union.
It publishes guidance, threat reports and cybersecurity research.
Its mandate is set by EU legislation and has evolved over time.
needs_review: Verify current legal mandate and programs using ENISA and EU sources.

item_description: Europol’s European Cybercrime Centre, which supports law enforcement cooperation against cybercrime.
item_facts: EC3 is part of the European Union Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation, Europol.
It provides operational and analytical support to investigations.
It works with national authorities and other partners.
needs_review: Verify current structure and activities using official Europol materials.

item_description: A division of the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation focused on investigating cyber threats and cyber-enabled crime.
item_facts: The FBI investigates cybercrime and national security cyber threats.
The Bureau works with domestic and international partners on cyber investigations.
It publishes public alerts and threat advisories.
needs_review: Verify current division structure and remit on FBI.gov.

item_description: France’s national cybersecurity agency, responsible for advising and supporting the security of government and critical systems.
item_facts: ANSSI is part of the French Prime Minister’s services.
It publishes technical recommendations and security alerts.
The agency supports the protection of state information systems and critical infrastructure.
needs_review: Verify current institutional placement and remit using ANSSI documentation.

item_description: Germany’s Federal Office for Information Security, the national authority for cyber and information security.
item_facts: BSI is a federal agency within Germany’s portfolio of the Federal Ministry of the Interior.
It publishes security advisories and technical standards.
It supports public administration, businesses and citizens.
needs_review: Verify current ministry relationship and responsibilities with official BSI sources.

item_description: An INTERPOL unit that supports international police cooperation on cybercrime investigations.
item_facts: INTERPOL helps police in member countries share information and coordinate action.
Its cybercrime work includes threat analysis and operational support.
The unit’s formal name and organizational structure may change.
needs_review: Confirm current official directorate name, remit and structure through INTERPOL sources.

item_description: An Israeli government body responsible for coordinating national cyber defense and strengthening cyber resilience.
item_facts: The Directorate coordinates national cyber defense efforts.
It provides guidance and services to organizations and the public.
Its formal name and responsibilities have changed over time.
needs_review: Verify current name, organizational placement and remit with official Israeli sources.

item_description: Japan’s National center of Incident readiness and Strategy for Cybersecurity, coordinating national cyber policy and response.
item_facts: NISC is part of Japan’s Cabinet Secretariat framework.
It coordinates cybersecurity policy across government.
Its organization and formal naming may evolve with government restructuring.
needs_review: Verify current Japanese agency name and institutional placement using government sources.

item_description: A South Korean public organization working on internet safety, information security and cyber incident response.
item_facts: KISA operates under South Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT.
It provides cyber incident response and security support.
Its work also covers internet and personal information protection.
needs_review: Verify current remit and ministry relationship on KISA and government websites.

item_description: A NATO-accredited center of excellence in Tallinn that studies cyber defense and supports training and exercises.
item_facts: The center is commonly abbreviated CCDCOE.
It is an international military organization accredited by NATO but is not itself a NATO command.
It organizes the annual Locked Shields cyber defense exercise.
needs_review: Verify membership, accreditation and exercise details on CCDCOE and NATO sites.

item_description: The United Kingdom’s National Cyber Security Centre, providing guidance and support to improve cyber security.
item_facts: The NCSC is part of GCHQ.
It publishes security guidance and threat information.
It supports government, businesses and the public.
needs_review: Verify current organizational relationship and services on NCSC.gov.uk.

item_description: The Dutch National Cyber Security Centre, which works to improve resilience and share threat information.
item_facts: The NCSC operates within the Dutch Ministry of Justice and Security framework.
It supports organizations designated as vital and central government.
Dutch national cyber organizations have undergone structural changes, so current naming matters.
needs_review: Verify current organization name, remit and ministerial placement using official Dutch sources.

item_description: New Zealand’s National Cyber Security Centre, providing cyber threat detection, advice and incident support.
item_facts: The NCSC is part of the Government Communications Security Bureau.
It works with organizations to improve cyber resilience.
It publishes information about cyber threats and incidents.
needs_review: Verify current structure and remit with official New Zealand government sources.

item_description: The U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, which develops measurement standards and widely used cybersecurity guidance.
item_facts: NIST is part of the U.S. Department of Commerce.
The NIST Cybersecurity Framework is used by organizations to manage cyber risk.
NIST publishes the Special Publication 800 series on information security.
needs_review: Verify current framework version and publication details on NIST.gov.

item_description: A U.S. National Security Agency directorate that works to protect national security systems and share cybersecurity guidance.
item_facts: The directorate was established in 2019.
It focuses on defending national security systems and the Defense Industrial Base.
NSA publishes technical cybersecurity advisories with partner agencies.
needs_review: Verify current directorate structure and remit on NSA.gov.

item_description: Singapore’s Cyber Security Agency, which leads national cybersecurity strategy and coordinates cyber resilience.
item_facts: CSA was established in 2015.
It is part of Singapore’s Prime Minister’s Office and supported by the Ministry of Digital Development and Information.
It oversees implementation of the Cybersecurity Act and national cyber programs.
needs_review: Verify current ministerial placement and statutory remit on CSA.gov.sg.
